criterion: Its cost is no longer quadratic in the number of sessions in one repository, shown by a measurement
summary: Measured on sequential non-overlapping sessions, which was the worst case for the pairwise version because nothing let it stop early: 500 sessions 0.140s to 0.001s (219x), 2000 sessions 2.259s to 0.003s (872x), 5000 sessions 14.463s to 0.007s (2097x), with the two implementations asserted to produce identical verdicts at each size. The growth is what matters: the old cost rose 103x between 500 and 5000 sessions while the new one rose 7x. Two thousand sessions is eleven a day across the six months the journal retains, so a single-checkout daily user reaches the old cost, where it was almost the whole runtime of a report. test_a_thousand_sequential_sessions_are_not_compared_pairwise keeps a loose bound in the suite. Five guards on this function, all reported pinned, including one that drops the self-exclusion and one that stops filtering unbounded sessions - both caught by the equivalence test rather than by a test written for them. Suites: 418 tests OK on 3.12.12 and 418 OK on 3.10.19; black and mypy clean over 37 files; sync_adapters --check passes.
